title: Under the table
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
logline: Wood tries to draw the dog. The dog does not hold still. Then he does.

panels.composition: Wood's table. WOOD trying to draw BARNABY, who is walking in a circle.
props: the circle drawn as motion lines

balloons.text: Hold still. Watterson could draw a tiger from memory. I have the real thing and he won't—

image.prompt: a young man at a drawing table trying to sketch a small dog that keeps walking in a circle, motion lines, black and white

panels.composition: The pad: six false starts of a dog, each one a different dog.

image.prompt: close-up of a drawing pad covered in six abandoned half-drawn sketches of a dog, each slightly different

panels.composition: Barnaby stops. Curls under the table into a tight ball, an ammonite. Asleep in one motion.

characters.pose: curled in a tight ball under the table

image.prompt: a scruffy dog curling into a tight spiral under a drawing table and falling instantly asleep

panels.composition: The pad: one drawing. The ball. Perfect. Wood's hand not moving, so as not to wake it.
props: the pad with one finished drawing of a curled dog

image.prompt: close-up of a finished brush-pen drawing of a dog curled into a tight ball, and a hand holding the pen very still above it, no words

art.line: brush-pen now — the weekday deadline teaches the hand to commit; still xeroxed, still black and white
art.paper: the college paper's newsprint; the digest's quarter-letter xerox

notes: The strip learns the dog's weight. Watterson invoked once; the strip means it.
